tool_args.draft_answer:
Based on EXHIBIT A: NIST SP 800-207 ZERO TRUST CONTROL PLANE & PEP TOPOLOGY in 02_Zero_Trust_Architecture_Specs.pdf (Section ZTA-NIST-800-207), the components interact as follows before granting enclave access:

1. Control Plane Evaluation: The Policy Engine (PE) evaluates continuous device posture, BeyondCorp context-aware access levels, and Chronicle threat intelligence feeds from the untrusted subject and device.
2. Control Plane Signaling & Token Issuance: The Policy Engine (PE) signals the Policy Administrator (PA) to mint short-lived mTLS / OIDC session tokens.
3. Data Plane Enforcement: The Data Plane Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)—comprising Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) and Envoy Service Mesh ingress gateways—terminates all untrusted traffic and permits per-request access to the protected enclave resources only upon PA verification.

There are no amendments superseding Section ZTA-NIST-800-207.
